Here’s a concise, fact-focused overview of the Women’s Team archery event at the London 2012 Summer Olympics.

Essential facts
- Venue: Lord’s Cricket Ground, London
- Dates: 27–29 July 2012 (ranking round on 27 July; eliminations and medal matches on 29 July)
- Competitors/Nations: 36 archers in 12 national teams (3 archers per team)
- Format:
  - Each archer shot a 72‑arrow ranking round; team seeds were based on the three scores combined.
  - Bracket of 12 teams: seeds 1–4 received byes to the quarterfinals; seeds 5–12 contested the 1/8 finals.
  - Match format (team rounds in 2012): cumulative scoring over 24 arrows per team (four ends of six arrows; each archer shoots two arrows per end), maximum 240 points.

Medalists
- Gold: South Korea (Ki Bo-bae, Lee Sung-jin, Choi Hyeon-ju)
- Silver: China (Cheng Ming, Fang Yuting, Xu Jing)
- Bronze: Japan (Kaori Kawanaka, Ren Hayakawa, Miki Kanie)

Medal matches and notable scores
- Gold medal match: South Korea def. China, 210–209 (a one-point thriller decided on the final arrows)
- Bronze medal match: Japan def. Russia, 209–207

Path to the podium (high-level)
- South Korea and China advanced through the quarterfinals and semifinals to meet in the final.
- Japan and Russia met in the bronze match after semifinal losses to China and South Korea, respectively.

Notable storylines
- South Korea extended its dominance in the Olympic women’s team event, winning the gold again in 2012. (The Korean women have never lost this event since it was introduced in 1988.)
- Japan’s bronze was a landmark achievement: the nation’s first Olympic medal in the women’s team event.

If you’d like, I can list all participating teams with seeds and round-by-round opponents and scores.
